The driver's assertion is exactly a no-show claim, so NS-1 governs rather than NS-3.

NS-1 requires three elements. (i) The driver pressed "I'm Here": the timeline shows the tap at 17:18:50 [F6], corroborated by the driver's chat message at 17:19 "I'm here at the pickup point" [F9]. (ii) The driver was at the pickup point per GPS at the moment of the tap: 38 m from the pickup point at the tap, with a closest approach of 34 m [F6][F1]; this is well inside the 200 m arrival radius used by the record [F2][RD-NS-1]. (iii) The driver waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup after the tap: the trace records 220 s (3 min 40 s) continuously inside the radius after the tap, until the cancellation [F6], and the chat confirms "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" at 17:22 [F10][RD-NS-1]. The platform likewise recorded arrival at 17:17:50 and cancellation 4 min 40 s later [F5], and the driver was stationary 17:18:25–17:22:30 at 53 m from the pickup [F3].

All three NS-1 conditions are met, so the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and the outcome is no_action [F7][F4][RD-NS-1]. Because there is no refundable amount under RD-2 (the case is not a route deviation, and no off-route segment facts exist), RD-6's flag_account is not triggered even though the driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days [F17][RD-6]; a profile fact can never stand alone, and here NS-1 is fully satisfied. The rider's complaint that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" is a statement against the system record: the GPS and timeline show the driver inside the radius for 4 min 40 s before cancelling and having waited 3 min 40 s after the tap [F5][F6][F3], so the record governs.

There is no threat, harassment, intimidation or dangerous-driving allegation, so no escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 is warranted.
